direction: Equation discovery under noise: recover the Lorenz-63 equations with sparse regression (sequentially thresholded least squares in numpy) from noisy trajectories, comparing how derivatives are obtained: finite differences, Savitzky-Golay smoothing, total-variation or spline smoothing, and the weak (integral) formulation. Measure the rate of exact support recovery and coefficient error as functions of noise level.

decisions.decision: First tuning grid hit edges (SG window 11 = smallest, STLSQ thr 0.6 = largest); extended grid to SG windows 5-161 and thr up to 0.8 and re-ran tuning on the same independent tuning seeds (1000-1004). dt=0.01 (1001 samples) instead of 0.002 to keep dense TV differentiation cheap.

First launch of the main runs had a shell bug (bash 3 has no associative arrays) that logged every system under the name 'Weak-form STLSQ'. Killed the launcher, removed those mislabeled main rows, raw files and logs, and re-ran all main runs with a fixed launcher. No results were inspected before the re-run.

CORRECTION to the earlier setup decision: the planned grid extension (SG windows 5,7; threshold 0.8) was never applied (the command did not run), so all tuned.json values and all runs use the original grid: SG window {11..161}, threshold {0.05..0.6}. The smallest SG window (11) and the largest threshold (0.6) are chosen at some noise levels, i.e. at the grid edge; this is reported as a limitation. dt=0.01 (1001 samples) is used instead of 0.002 for cost.
research.yaml ablations list the run names (kind=ablation) in groups sweep_width, abl_p, abl_libstate, sweep_thr, as rh check matches on name

Audit fix: the tuner resolved exact ties (identical models on all 5 tuning trajectories) by grid order, i.e. the smallest threshold; this decided the threshold in 19 of 30 system x noise cells (all cells at 0-1%, weak 2%, FD 5%, FD 10%, spline 10%), not only FD at 5%. New rule: support rate, then median error, then the LARGEST threshold on an exact tie (sparser model), same for all systems, same 5 tuning seeds and grids. Old tuned values kept in method/tuned_v1.json. All main runs, the width sweep and exponent ablation are superseded and re-run; abl_libstate cells (SG/spline at 2,5%) are unchanged by the re-tune and kept. The threshold sweep is redone as one run per system x level x seed evaluating all 5 thresholds on the same regression problem (diagnostic, test seeds).

Audit fix round: tuner tie rule changed to largest threshold on exact ties (deterministic, no test data), all main/width/exponent runs re-run, threshold-grid diagnostic for all systems and levels; first-version runs kept as superseded and both choices shown in the paper. H1 and H2 refuted, H3 supported, H4 partly, H5 not supported.

Audit round 2: the tuner's rule (support rate, median error, largest threshold) is kept as run; only its description is corrected (a tie is equal rate and equal median, not identical models). A new diagnostic, method/tie_check.py, checks model identity of tied configurations on the tuning seeds and what a mean-error tie-break would select. The rule is not changed a third time because the mean-error rule selects the same configuration in all 30 cells, so no run would change.

Fix round 2: tie criterion described as implemented and checked by tie_check.py; abstract/conclusion caveats for H2 and coefficient error; one statement of resolution; exponent errors in text. Tie table and exponent table left out of the paper to stay at 6 pages.
